question: How many of the people in a workplace or organization does a typical member actually know, by the size of the place? At what size does sharing a workplace (or a legislative chamber, or a party chapter) stop meaning you know everyone in it, and how quickly does a new member of a state legislature come to know the other members?

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Contact frequency and what changes a relationship, not how many colleagues a person knows.

sourcesChecked.whatItSettled: State contact/help/member incidence, not per-tie survival or invitation calendar.

sourcesChecked.source: Pew Research Center2025 social connections; probability survey6204 US adults
sourcesChecked.whatItSettled: Weekly friend contact benchmark with mode and denominator; Pew notices/disclaimer retained.

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Redistribution/game derivative table grant not established; no data extracted.

title: How many colleagues a person knows, and when a big workplace stops being everyone you know
usableAnswer: A size threshold or a curve (share of colleagues known by organization size), from workplace network or organizational sociology studies; for legislatures, anything on how quickly freshmen come to know the chamber.
whyItMatters: People counts everyone in a player's workplace or group as somebody they know. After winning a Texas House seat, a playtest character had 181 'Work' acquaintances on the first day (2026-09-23). src/presentation/people-directory.ts EVERYBODY_KNOWS_EVERYBODY_LIMIT now treats a place with more than 20 other people as people to meet, known only once something is on the record between them. The 20 is a PLACEHOLDER.

findings.findings: Workplace/legislature/chapter membership does not establish acquaintance. Team overlap, repeated co-presence, introductions and prior ties supply actual routes to knowing colleagues.
findings.estimate: Pew friendship counts cannot replace coworkers-known by firm size; no defensible numeric size cap or new-legislator acquaintance time identified.
findings.gaps: Request remains empirical gap; any current cap stays registered tunable, with no claim that every member knows everyone.
